features.title: Draft a document from a prompt
features.summary: Tell Copilot what you need and it writes a first draft in your document. You then keep it, discard it or refine it with a follow-up.
steps: Open a document in Word.
Select the Copilot Dynamic Action Button in the corner of the document.
Copilot opens in the chat pane with Edit mode on.
Type a prompt describing the outcome you want and point Copilot to any source material.
Review the result, then keep it, discard it, or refine it with a follow-up prompt.
prompts: Draft a customer brief about [initiative] for [audience].
Create an outline for a project update with sections for status, milestones, risks, and decisions needed.
Add a short conclusion with next steps.
limits: Needs an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and/or Microsoft Copilot license, and may be switched off by your organisation's settings.
Supports fewer languages than the Word interface.
Works within Word and your Microsoft 365 content. It does not connect to external tools.

features.title: Pull in your own files, emails or meetings
features.summary: Point Copilot at a document, email or meeting so the draft uses that material instead of guessing.
steps: Open Copilot in Word from the Copilot Dynamic Action Button.
In the chat pane, type / and start typing the name of a document, email or meeting.
Pick the item from the list.
Write your request, for example to summarise or build on it.
prompts: Draft a one-page summary of the project in /[file name] for my manager.
Create an outline for a project update using /[meeting name].
What decisions are needed before this document is ready to share?
limits: You need permission to open the item you reference.
On Word for iPad, the Draft with Copilot dialog lets you attach up to three files with Reference a file, and this needs a Microsoft Copilot subscription. I did not find a desktop limit stated.
Availability depends on your licence, organisation settings and platform.

features.title: Rewrite or tighten text you already have
features.summary: Select a passage and ask Copilot to rewrite it, shorten it or change the tone. For bigger changes, describe them in the chat pane.
steps: Open Copilot in Word.
Select the text you want to change.
Choose Rewrite for a quick change to that passage.
For a larger change, describe it in the chat pane instead.
In a shared document, Copilot shows a preview of suggested changes in chat. Nothing is added until you approve it.
prompts: Make this section more concise and customer-ready without changing the meaning.
Reorganize this section so the problems, risks and next steps are easier to follow.
Rewrite this paragraph in a more formal tone.
limits: Always read the result. Copilot content is AI-generated and can be wrong.
Needs an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and/or Microsoft Copilot license.
Supports fewer languages than the Word interface.

features.title: Summarise a document and ask questions about it
features.summary: Get the key points of a long document, or ask Copilot what is unclear, without changing the file.
steps: Open the document in Word and open Copilot.
Select Chat only so Copilot answers in chat and makes no changes to the document.
Ask for a summary or ask a question about the content.
A summary may also appear at the top of the page when you open a document, depending on your settings and license.
prompts: Summarize this document in five bullets.
What decisions are needed before this document is ready to share?
What parts of this document may be unclear to a customer?
limits: The automatic summary at the top of the page depends on your settings and licence.
Check key facts against the document. Summaries can miss detail.
Needs an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and/or Microsoft Copilot license.

features.title: Ask Copilot to analyse or edit your workbook
features.summary: Open Copilot in Excel and describe the task in plain words. It can edit the workbook directly, show a plan first, or just answer questions.
steps: Select the Copilot icon in the lower-right corner of Excel.
Choose a mode: Allow editing (the default), Plan, or Chat only.
Describe the task in plain language.
In Plan mode, review and confirm the plan before Copilot changes anything.
Select the Stop button on the right of the chat input field if you need to halt a task.
prompts: Summarize the feedback in A2:A20.
Classify each sentiment entry in B2:B100 and add the result in a new column.
Create a PivotTable with the sum of sales, with month in rows and category in columns.
limits: Edit, chat and plan modes work on Excel for Windows, Mac and the web.
On iPad, chat and plan work and edit mode is described as rolling out to production. On iPhone and Android it is chat only (iPhone edit also rolling out).
Copilot may not be included in your subscription or may be restricted by your organisation.

source.label: Get started with Copilot in Excel

features.title: Agent Mode: multi-step workbook jobs
features.summary: Agent Mode lets Copilot plan and carry out several steps in one go, such as reshaping data, merging sheets or building a report. Microsoft's page now describes it as the Allow editing mode inside Copilot in Excel.
steps: Select the Copilot icon in the lower-right corner of Excel.
Check the mode is Allow editing, which the page says supports complex, multi-step tasks.
Describe the whole job in one prompt.
Watch the changes. Select Stop on the right of the chat input field to pause.
Switch to Plan mode if you want to approve the steps first.
prompts: Create a dashboard styled with our @brandkit.
Merge the sales sheets into one table and add a total per region.
Build a one-page report from this data with a chart for each month.
limits: The original Agent Mode support page was titled as a Frontier preview. The current Copilot in Excel pages list editing as available on Windows, Mac and web without preview wording, but I could not find a Microsoft page that announces the move to general release, so check with your admin.
On iPad and iPhone, edit mode is described as rolling out to production.
Always check the numbers it produces against your source data.

features.title: Get insights, charts and PivotTables
features.summary: Ask Copilot to spot trends and outliers in your data, or to build a chart or PivotTable for you.
steps: Make sure your data is in an Excel table and select a cell inside it.
Select the Copilot icon in the lower-right corner of Excel.
Ask for insights, or name the format you want, such as a PivotTable or a chart.
Add a single chart to a sheet, or add all insights to a new sheet, and undo if it is not right.
prompts: Create a PivotTable with the sum of sales, with month in rows and category in columns.
Highlight the top 10 values in column D in green.
Show me trends and outliers in this table.
limits: Your data needs to be in an Excel table for this to work well.
The Get started page does not list size limits. Check the Visualize your data page for specifics.
Review everything Copilot generates before you share it.

source.label: Visualize your data with Copilot in Excel

features.title: Create a presentation from a prompt
features.summary: Describe the deck you want and Copilot builds it. It may ask about audience, length, template and images first.
steps: Start a new presentation in PowerPoint.
Select the Copilot icon at the bottom-right corner of the screen to open Copilot Chat.
Leave the model selector on Auto unless you want to choose one.
If your organisation requires a Brand Kit, choose one in Select brand.
Describe the presentation in the prompt box and answer or skip Copilot's clarifying questions.
prompts: Create a presentation about the history of soccer.
Create a 7-slide executive brief on [your topic], with a title slide, key insights, risks and mitigations, and next steps.
Add a slide about [topic].
limits: Needs an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and/or Microsoft Copilot license.
Copilot builds from your selected template. Start from your organisation's template to keep its look.
AI-generated content can be wrong. Review every slide.

source.label: Create a new presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint

features.title: Turn a Word document into a deck
features.summary: Point Copilot at a Word document and it turns it into slides.
steps: Open the Copilot pane.
Type or select Create presentation from file in the suggested prompt menu.
Search your files or paste the URL of a Word document.
Review the slides Copilot builds.
prompts: Create presentation from file
Create a presentation from /[Word document name] for a 10-minute briefing.
Add a slide summarising the risks in this document.
limits: Works best with Word documents smaller than 24 MB.
Use Word Styles (such as headings) so Copilot can split the document into slides.
Needs a Microsoft Copilot (work) licence for the file route.

source.label: Create a new presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint

features.title: Edit with Copilot (plan, change, review)
features.summary: Edit with Copilot (formerly called Agent Mode) takes natural-language requests and plans, makes and reviews changes across a deck, such as restructuring it or rewriting slides for clarity.
steps: Open your Office app and sign in with a Copilot-enabled account.
In the Copilot prompt box, select Tools, then select Edit with Copilot.
Type a clear request with specific details.
Wait while Copilot builds the content, then review it.
prompts: Create a 7-slide executive brief on [your topic], with a title slide, key insights, risks and mitigations, and next steps.
Rewrite these slides so they can be presented in five minutes.
Restructure this deck so the recommendation comes first.
limits: A Microsoft Tech Community post (March 2026) said it was on the web first with desktop rollout coming and made-default-on coming. I could not confirm current desktop status, so I tagged it cautiously as preview.
It uses templates from the Organization Asset Library or Copilot Brand Kits, or can work without a template.
Microsoft's support page says editing with Copilot uses Anthropic models, while the Tech Community post said OpenAI at the time. Treat model details as changing.

source.label: Get started editing with Copilot in Office

features.title: Change the design, add images, summarise
features.summary: Ask Copilot to restyle the whole deck, add a slide or a picture, or list the main ideas of a presentation.
steps: Open the Copilot pane.
To restyle, ask Copilot to Try a new design. You can repeat it until you like the style.
To add content, ask for a new slide or an image in a prompt.
To get the main points, ask Copilot to Summarize this presentation.
prompts: Try a new design.
Add a slide about the history of Women's Olympic Soccer.
Add an image of a store under construction.
Summarize this presentation.
limits: Needs an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and/or Microsoft Copilot license.
The Organize this presentation feature was being retired on 14 July 2025, so do not rely on it.
The page gives no numeric limits. Copilot output may be unexpected or inaccurate, so verify it.

issues.text: Copilot in Word supports fewer languages than Word itself, and may be off if your organisation has restricted it.
The COPILOT function was removed from 14 September 2026. Cells that recalculate show #NAME?, while old results stay as saved values.
Edit mode on Excel for iPad and iPhone is described as rolling out to production. iPhone and Android are chat only.

source.label: Get started with Copilot in Excel

issues.text: Brand kits have reportedly disappeared, failed to open or stopped appearing. No fix date was given.

source.label: PowerPoint: Edit with Copilot, Brand Kit and image gen overview

changes.text: The COPILOT function stopped being available in Excel. Use Copilot in Excel chat instead.
